result.title: CodeHOI: Code with Agents for Physically Plausible 4D Hand-Object Interaction
result.summary: Modeling 4D hand-object interaction (HOI) is fundamental to understanding manipulation. This requires physics, since hands move objects only by touch and each material responds differently. Yet existing methods ignore this physics or simulate only a narrow range of matter. Programs can instead describe any matter with its physics, but coding agents omit the hand that drives the interaction. We close this gap with CodeHOI, to our knowledge the first agentic framework that writes physically plausible 4D HOI as programs. To write one, an Object Agent first builds each object with the physics of its matter. An HOI Agent then specifies the hands by their contacts and simulates each kind of matter with an established physics solver. Finally, an Evaluator Agent checks each result against physical laws. We also introduce CodeHOI-Bench with 100 reconstruction and generation tasks across four kinds of matter. With off-the-shelf frontier models, CodeHOI writes interactions that are plausible for every kind of matter and remain so when transferred to an independent physics engine. It thereby enables coding agents to write physically plausible HOI across diverse matter.

AI.brief_summary: CodeHOI 让多个编程 agent 分工写出带物理属性的物体与手部接触程序，并借物理求解器生成物理上合理的 4D 手物交互，同时提出覆盖四类材质的基准。
AI.relevance_reason: 工作属于图形学/机器人方向的物理仿真与代码生成，虽含 Evaluator 校验环节，但对象是仿真程序而非 VLM 的 latent 推理状态或视觉证据使用，缺乏可核查的状态、训练或决策联系。
